cards.text: We're back at Shiloh, friend, where Eli the priest has two sons who serve as priests too. And the text doesn't warm us up. No preheating the oven, nothing: it says the sons of Eli were wicked men, and they had no regard for the LORD.

cards.question: Eli's sons had no regard for the LORD, but they did respect the custom of the priests with the people.

cards.text: So here's what they do. When any man offers a sacrifice, the priest's servant comes over while the meat is still boiling, and he's carrying something.

cards.question: What does the priest's servant bring over to the boiling sacrifice?

cards.text: He plunges that fork into the pan or kettle or cauldron or cooking pot. This man is NOT picky, friend. If it's boiling, he's in it.

cards.question: Whatever the meat fork brings up out of the pot, the priest claims it for ___.
The fork in the pot isn't a one-time thing at Shiloh. Who gets treated this way?

cards.text: It gets worse. Even before the fat is burned, the servant walks up to the man sacrificing with a demand, like somebody reaching into my oven before the timer even goes off.

cards.question: Before the fat is even burned, what does the servant demand from the man sacrificing?

answers.text: Raw meat for the priest to roast
A second animal for the priest
A share of grain for the priest

cards.text: Some men push back. They say the fat must be burned first, and then the servant can take whatever he wants. Fair deal, right? You'd THINK so.

cards.question: When a man says to burn the fat first, how does the servant answer him?

answers.text: Give it now or I take it by force
Fine but the priest wants extra
Then the priest will take none

cards.question: The LORD sees the sin of Eli's sons as severe.
Eli's sons were treating the LORD's offering with ___.

cards.text: Now step away from all that grabbing and take a breath, friend. The boy Samuel is ministering before the LORD, wearing a linen ephod.
Each year his mother Hannah comes up with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice. And she brings Samuel something she made for him.

cards.question: What does Hannah make for Samuel and bring to him each year?

cards.text: And each year Eli blesses Elkanah and Hannah. He says may the LORD give them children by Hannah in place of the one she dedicated to the LORD.

cards.question: The LORD attends to Hannah after Eli's blessing. How many more children does she have?

cards.text: Five more kids. FIVE. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.
Now Eli is very old, and he hears about everything his sons are doing to all Israel. He even hears that they're sleeping with the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: Eli confronts his sons about everything he's heard. What does he ask them?

answers.text: Why are you doing these things
Who told you this was allowed
How long has this gone on

cards.text: He says he hears about their wicked deeds from all these people, and it's not a good report going around among the LORD's people. Friend, when the whole group chat is talking about you, it's never good news.

cards.question: Eli warns his sons that God can intercede when a man sins against another man. But if a man sins against ___, who can intercede for him?
Eli's sons take their father's warning to heart and listen to him.

cards.text: And the text tells us why they wouldn't listen: the LORD intended to put them to death. That's a heavy line, friend.

cards.question: Meanwhile, the boy Samuel keeps growing in stature. How else is he growing?

answers.text: In favor with the LORD and with man
In trouble with Eli and his sons
In charge of the priests' servants

cards.text: Then a man of God comes to Eli with a word from the LORD. The LORD reminds Eli that He clearly revealed Himself to Eli's father's house back when they were in Egypt under Pharaoh's house.

cards.question: Out of all the tribes of Israel, what did the LORD select Eli's father to be?

cards.text: The LORD even gave Eli's father's house all the food offerings of the Israelites. So He asks Eli why he kicks at the sacrifice and offering He prescribed for His dwelling place.

cards.question: The LORD tells Eli that he has honored his ___ more than Him.

cards.text: They've been fattening themselves on the best of all the offerings of His people Israel. The LORD had said Eli's house would walk before Him forever, but now He declares, Far be it from Me!

cards.question: The LORD says He will honor those who honor Him. What does He say about those who despise Him?

cards.text: Then comes the judgment. The LORD will cut off the strength of Eli's house so no one in it reaches old age, and all his descendants will die by the sword of men.

cards.question: The LORD gives Eli a sign about his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. What is it?

answers.text: They will both die on the same day
They will both be sent far away
They will both be stripped of rank

cards.text: But the message doesn't stop there. The LORD says He will raise up a faithful priest for Himself and build for him an enduring house.

cards.question: What does the LORD say this faithful priest will do?

answers.text: Whatever is in the LORD's heart and mind
Whatever the people of Israel ask him
Whatever the house of Eli tells him

cards.question: Everyone left in Eli's house will come bow down to that faithful priest and plead to be appointed to some ___ office.

cards.text: And that's where the man of God's message ends. Trust me, friend, this story is FAR from over.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The card says Eli's two sons 'serve as priests too.' The passage never says this. The fact comes from 1 Samuel 1:3, but the card cites only 1 Samuel 2:12, so the outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The text is conditional: 'And if any man said to him, "The fat must be burned first..."' (1 Sam 2:16). The card makes it an event that happened: 'Some men push back.' Card 11 repeats the shift with 'When a man says.'
This is Samuel's first appearance in the lesson. He shows up only as 'The boy Samuel,' with nothing to say who he is, such as the son Hannah dedicated to the LORD.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 2 fill in the blank, with three multiple choice cards in a row (cards 7, 9, 11).

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 multiple choice, 3 fill in the blank and 1 true or false, with cards 13, 15 and 17 all multiple choice.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The question already says God can intercede when a man sins against another man. The wrong answers 'his brother' and 'a stranger' are both just 'another man,' so the setup rules them out. They also mean nearly the same as the first half of the contrast, and a baker could argue them.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'They've been fattening themselves' can be read as the sons only. The LORD says it to Eli: 'You have honored your sons more than Me by fattening yourselves' (1 Sam 2:29). Eli is included in the charge, and the card blurs that.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card leaves out that the faithful priest 'will walk before My anointed one for all time' (1 Sam 2:35). No other card covers it, so the baker misses a key detail of the promise.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: No card covers the rest of 1 Samuel 2:36: Eli's house will bow down 'for a piece of silver or a morsel of bread' and plead for an office 'so that I can eat a piece of bread.' The house that fattened itself on the offerings ends up begging for bread, and the baker never hears it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The story-continues line, 'Trust me, friend, this story is FAR from over,' nearly copies the doc's example line, 'Trust me, friend, this story's not done.'

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Most story cards in this stop (cards 8, 10, 12, 14, 16) read as close retellings of the verses with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 3 has the only comic beat in the stop.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
